description: `!{}`-guarded handlers inside a `<match>` arm (RT). #one: `{ risky() !{…} }` — the .Empty arm sets @r = 1. #seq: the guard followed by `; @msg = "y"` — the arm adds 10 and the second statement runs. Before S440 the arm's handler statement parse threw (null parent block) and was swallowed, so both handlers emitted a bare `_scrml_risky();`: the guard AND the trailing statement were dropped at exit 0.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S439 #14 + S440 "all recs" (restore conformance); review:S440-fix-round-F3
rationale: §5.2.3 — on each dispatch the statements of an inline block SHALL run in source order, and no statement SHALL be dropped whatever its position, including inside a `<match>`/engine arm. §19.4.3 — a `!{}` guard is how a handler handles a failable call; a guard the checker counts as handling the call must also be emitted.
